edit.description: the package's declaration of the engine's per-entry refusal
the refusal reaches the chain the factory builds
the three fates by mode and anchor
the declaration arrives on the chain

summary: the default handoff re-dispatches an entry whose latest attempt was a clean exit at the current HEAD — the same dispatch against an unchanged world, for the same outcome
acceptance: the package declares the engine's per-entry refusal, and an entry whose latest prior attempt is a clean exit at the tick's own HEAD is not handed to build while one at an older HEAD still is.
tests: an entry whose latest clean exit is at the current HEAD is not handed to build
an entry whose latest clean exit is at an older HEAD is handed to build
an entry whose latest attempt is a gate revert at the current HEAD is handed to build
notes: Read from the mode and the anchor the engine reports on the record — PriorAttempt's `mode` and `headSha` (src/Prompt.ts) — never a heuristic of the package's own. Only clean-exit qualifies; every other mode describes a world the next tick can change. The capability shipped at 908ce206; this is the policy half build's note named.

edit.description: standing refusals look up by the engine's entry-attempt key instead of filtering on a hand-spelled keyspace and slug
the agreement over a tag slugify rewrites

summary: the inbox slice re-spells the engine's record keying by hand — an "entry" keyspace literal beside its own slugify of each queued tag — so a keying change stops the slice waking, silently

per.section: The fix lands at the mechanism

acceptance: the slice reaches each queued entry's standing record through the engine's own `entryAttemptKey`, and no keyspace literal or slug of a tag is spelled in the package beside it.
pins: the inbox slice's standing refusals key a tag slugify rewrites the way the engine's own entry-attempt key does
notes: From build's note on THE-PICKABLE-SET-CARRIES-A-CHAIN-DECLARED-REFUSAL. The filter direction is what made `entryAttemptKey` look like a non-drop-in: iterating the queue and looking up in `ctx.priorAttempts` is the same set, since the map holds one record per written identity. `entryAttemptKey` is exported from src/priorAttempts.ts.
